title: Survival Island: Stranded
theme: Stranded on a tropical island after a shipwreck
description: Your cargo ship has gone down in a storm. You have washed ashore on an uncharted island with two fellow survivors. With no radio, no rescue guarantee, and dwindling supplies, every decision you make could mean the difference between survival and catastrophe. Choose wisely: help may be farther away than you think.
learning_objectives: Understand how to evaluate risk versus reward in high-stakes situations with incomplete information
Practice resource management by balancing competing priorities under scarcity
Learn how group dynamics, morale, and cooperation affect survival outcomes
Develop strategic thinking by planning multiple steps ahead rather than reacting impulsively
Explore how knowledge and skill-building compound over time to improve long-term outcomes

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: You are a survivor washed ashore on an uncharted tropical island after your cargo ship sank
Each round presents a new survival challenge requiring a strategic decision
Monitor your seven resources: Health, Energy, Food, Water, Shelter Quality, Morale, and Knowledge
Your choices affect not only the current round but echo through later rounds via callbacks
At three major branch points (Rounds 4, 8, and 12) your decision opens a different path
Reach the final rounds with enough resources to attempt rescue signaling
tips: Water is the most critical resource -- dehydration kills faster than starvation
Knowledge compounds -- investing time to learn skills pays off in later rounds
Alex and Sam represent different survival philosophies; observe their outcomes
High energy enables bolder actions; exhaustion leads to poor choices
Morale affects how well you and your companions work together

competitors.description: Alex moves fast and takes bold gambles. High risk, high reward -- but sometimes at a cost.

You are severely dehydrated. Finding water is now your only priority.

halftime_config.reflection_question: You have survived ten days on this island. Looking back at your decisions, which choice are you most proud of -- and which would you change if you could?

When you consume fewer calories than your body burns, leading to weight loss and eventually weakness.
Water that is safe to drink -- free of harmful bacteria, parasites, and contaminants.

The localized climate conditions inside or immediately around your shelter, which you can actively manage for warmth or cooling.

rounds.title: Day 1 Morning: Washed Ashore
rounds.story:
Salt water burns your throat as you claw your way up the sand. The cargo ship MV Meridian is gone -- swallowed by last night's storm in minutes. Around you, waves deposit splintered wood, tangled rope, and the occasional sealed container. Two other survivors, Alex and Sam, are already on their feet. Alex is hauling a heavy cargo case out of the surf. Sam is scanning the treeline with sharp, measuring eyes.

You have the clothes on your back, a waterproof lighter that miraculously still works, and perhaps twenty minutes before the rising tide swallows your access to the wreckage. Every second you spend here is a second the debris floats farther out of reach.

This is day one. The choices you make in the next hour will shape every day that follows.
rounds.setting: A sandy cove flanked by volcanic rock. The wreckage of MV Meridian bobs two hundred metres offshore. Jungle begins twenty metres from the high-tide line.
rounds.challenge: Maximize what you salvage from the wreck before the tide rises and debris disperses.
rounds.goal: Secure critical supplies from the shipwreck debris before the opportunity is gone.

scene_hint.location: Sandy cove with volcanic rock outcrops
scene_hint.weather: overcast, waves still choppy
scene_hint.objects: ship wreckage debris, cargo containers, driftwood, tangled rope, foam coolers
scene_hint.character_positions: survivor standing knee-deep in surf, two others working nearby
scene_hint.mood: desperate urgency, raw survival instinct

choices.label: Swim to the Wreckage
choices.description: Risk the choppy surf to reach the ship's hull and grab sealed supplies before they sink.

consequence_scene.headline: Jackpot from the Deep!
consequence_scene.description: A sealed emergency kit: protein bars, a water filtration straw, flares, and a folding knife. The risk paid off.

choices.label: Collect Debris on the Shore
choices.description: Stay on the beach and systematically collect everything washing in -- rope, wood, containers.

consequence_scene.headline: Smart Salvage!
consequence_scene.description: Solid timber, rope, a tarp, and a dented but usable metal pot. Not glamorous, but exactly what shelter-building needs.

choices.label: Scout the Jungle Edge
choices.description: Let Alex and Sam handle the debris while you assess the island and look for fresh water immediately.

consequence_scene.headline: You Found a Stream!
consequence_scene.description: A freshwater stream just inside the treeline. Critical knowledge -- but Alex eyes you with suspicion. 'Glad you were so helpful with the salvage,' they say flatly.

rounds.image_prompt: a desolate beach at dawn, waves lapping at splintered wood and tangled ropes, two figures searching the shoreline, a heavy cargo case partially submerged in the surf, golden sunlight breaking through clouds
rounds.coaching_moment: Consider how this choice affects your long-term resources, not just the immediate gain.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What tradeoff did this decision reveal? What did you gain, and what did you give up?

expert_pick.reason: Resilience research shows that processing setbacks openly builds stronger teams.

rounds.title: Day 1 Afternoon: The First Camp
rounds.story:
The sun is climbing and the island heat is punishing. You have a rough pile of salvage on the beach but no shelter, no fire, and the jungle is beginning to make sounds you cannot identify. Alex wants to build a big signal fire on the beach immediately -- 'Get rescued today,' they insist. Sam disagrees: 'We need shelter and water first. A fire won't matter if we're dead from exposure.'

You look at the sky. Clouds are building on the horizon. If it rains tonight without shelter, hypothermia is a real risk even in the tropics. But if there is a passing ship or aircraft, a fire today might be your best chance at early rescue.

The group looks at you. Someone has to decide.
rounds.setting: Open beach near the cove. Salvage is piled on the sand. Jungle is close. Dark clouds building in the west.
rounds.challenge: Allocate the group's limited afternoon energy between shelter, fire, or water.
rounds.goal: Set the group's survival priorities before nightfall.

scene_hint.location: Open beach with salvage pile
scene_hint.weather: sunny with threatening clouds building on horizon
scene_hint.objects: salvage pile, driftwood, palm trees, small rock formations
scene_hint.character_positions: three survivors in discussion around the salvage pile, one pointing at jungle, one pointing at sea
scene_hint.mood: tense group debate, urgency of survival decisions

choices.label: Build Shelter First
choices.description: Spend the afternoon constructing a basic lean-to from the salvaged tarp and timber.

consequence_scene.headline: Shelter Before Sundown!
consequence_scene.description: A solid lean-to is ready before the first raindrops fall. When the downpour hits at midnight, you stay dry. Alex admits it was the right call.

choices.label: Light a Signal Fire
choices.description: Use the lighter to build a large smoke fire on the beach -- maximize visibility to passing vessels.

consequence_scene.headline: Smoke Seen -- But No One Comes
consequence_scene.description: A distant vessel appears on the horizon but changes course. The rain at night soaks everyone. Morale from the false hope, however, keeps spirits up through the miserable night.

choices.label: Divide and Conquer
choices.description: Send Alex to build shelter, Sam to fetch water, and you to gather firewood and food from the jungle edge.

consequence_scene.headline: A Functioning Camp!
consequence_scene.description: The group pulls together beautifully. By dusk you have shelter, water, a small fire, and coconuts. Sam raises an eyebrow: 'We might actually be okay.'

rounds.image_prompt: a sun-drenched beach with a chaotic pile of salvage, looming dark clouds on the horizon, two figures debating urgently, tall jungle trees whispering ominously nearby, tension in the air
rounds.coaching_moment: Think about trade-offs: what are you giving up to get this benefit?

expert_pick.reason: Leadership experts recommend thinking several moves ahead before committing.

rounds.title: Day 2: Message in a Bottle
rounds.story: Morning light filters through the palm fronds. Sam wakes you before dawn, holding something extraordinary: a glass bottle with a cork stopper and a rolled sheet of paper inside. It must have washed in during last night's rain. The handwriting is hurried but legible.
rounds.setting: Your camp on the beach, early morning. The bottle sits on a flat rock by the camp fire.
rounds.challenge: Interpret and act on the information in the mysterious message.
rounds.goal: Use the message's information to improve your chances of survival or rescue.

scene_hint.location: Small camp with lean-to shelter, morning mist
scene_hint.weather: calm, dewy, post-rain freshness
scene_hint.objects: glass bottle with paper inside, campfire embers, palm-frond shelter, makeshift log seats
scene_hint.character_positions: two survivors leaning over a rock examining the bottle, one reading by firelight
scene_hint.mood: mysterious hope, cautious curiosity

newspaper_content.headline: Message in a Bottle
newspaper_content.body: To anyone who finds this: I was stranded on this island for 31 days in 2019. There is a freshwater lagoon 3 km northeast of the main cove. The eastern cliffs have caves -- dry, safe from storms. Rescue ships pass the southern reef on Thursdays. BUILD A HIGH SIGNAL FIRE on the southern cliffs on Wednesday night. Good luck. -- J. Torres

choices.label: Head Northeast for the Lagoon
choices.description: Trust the message and make the trek to secure a reliable freshwater source.

consequence_scene.headline: The Lagoon Is Real!
consequence_scene.description: A crystal-clear freshwater lagoon, ringed with fruit trees. Your water crisis is solved indefinitely. The message was real -- and trustworthy.

choices.label: Scout the Eastern Caves
choices.description: Relocate camp to the cave system for permanent storm-proof shelter.

consequence_scene.headline: Cave Shelter Secured!
consequence_scene.description: The caves are exactly as described -- dry, elevated, with a view of the sea. Moving camp here fundamentally improves your long-term odds.

choices.label: Plan for Thursday's Rescue Ship
choices.description: Focus all energy on preparing a massive Wednesday night signal fire on the southern cliffs.

consequence_scene.headline: Today Is Monday -- Three Days Away
consequence_scene.description: You have time to prepare but must survive until then. The others agree to focus on building a massive fire cache. Hope is high -- but three days is a long time.

rounds.image_prompt: a serene beach at dawn, soft morning light filtering through palm fronds, a young person holding a glass bottle with a cork, gentle waves lapping at the shore
rounds.coaching_moment: How might your team react to this decision? What about your customers?
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why did you choose this option? What were you trying to protect or grow?

expert_pick.reason: Calculated risk-taking is what separates growth-oriented leaders from status-quo managers.

rounds.title: Day 3: The Fork in the Path
rounds.story:
On your third morning, the island reveals itself more clearly. From a rocky overlook you can see three distinct zones: a dense interior jungle, a sheltered southern bay with the cliffs the message mentioned, and a reef-ringed northern coast where you spotted what looked like a fishing vessel in the distance. Alex has already made their mind up: head north, try to flag the boat. Sam wants to go south and begin systematic rescue prep at the cliffs. You could also stay and spend the day fortifying camp and gathering resources.

This is the moment your survival strategy truly branches. Where you invest your energy today will determine the shape of the days to come.
rounds.setting: A rocky overlook with a panoramic view of the island and surrounding sea. Wind is picking up.
rounds.challenge: Choose the strategic direction that will define your survival path for the next several days.
rounds.goal: Commit to a survival strategy at a critical decision point.

scene_hint.location: Rocky volcanic ridge, panoramic ocean view
scene_hint.weather: clear and windy, good visibility
scene_hint.objects: volcanic rock ridge, distant fishing vessel on horizon, jungle canopy below, southern cliffs visible
scene_hint.character_positions: three survivors standing on ridge looking out in different directions, tension between them
scene_hint.mood: pivotal moment, dramatic fork in the road, hope and uncertainty

choices.label: Go North: Signal the Fishing Vessel
choices.description: Race to the northern coast to try to flag down the distant boat -- your best immediate rescue chance.

consequence_scene.headline: The Boat Is Gone -- But You Mapped the Coast
consequence_scene.description: By the time you reach the northern reef, the vessel has moved on. But you now have a detailed mental map of the northern coast and spotted a coconut grove.

choices.label: Go South: Establish Rescue Post
choices.description: Head to the southern cliffs and begin systematic preparation for the Thursday rescue ship.

consequence_scene.headline: Rescue Post Established!
consequence_scene.description: The southern cliffs are perfect. You begin a cache of dry wood for Wednesday night's fire. Sam builds a reflective signal mirror from salvage. Thursday feels achievable.

choices.label: Stay: Fortify Camp and Gather Resources
choices.description: Invest the day in camp improvement, food gathering, and tool-making before committing to any direction.

consequence_scene.headline: A Stronger Base
consequence_scene.description: Your camp is now genuinely comfortable. Alex is frustrated -- 'We're not here to live here!' -- but Sam nods. 'A good base means every future expedition starts stronger.'

rounds.image_prompt: a rocky overlook with a panoramic view of a dense jungle, a tranquil southern bay with steep cliffs, and a distant northern coast featuring a fishing vessel, bright sunlight illuminating the scene
rounds.coaching_moment: Look at your current resource levels — which constraint are you trying to address?

expert_pick.reason: Leadership experts recommend thinking several moves ahead before committing.

rounds.title: Day 4: The Northern Coast (Aggressive Path)
rounds.story:
The northern coast is dramatic -- towering sea stacks, crashing surf, and a coconut grove so dense it seems designed for castaways. Alex is exhilarated, already climbing a palm tree barefoot at alarming speed. You found three useful items washed into a sea cave: a partially intact life raft (deflated but repairable), a flare gun with one cartridge, and a dented metal tin of biscuits.

Alex wants to repair the raft and sail it around the reef to intercept passing vessels -- a bold, dangerous plan. You could also use this day to harvest the coconut grove thoroughly and cache food for the group. Or spend time studying the currents and tides to make any future water-based escape safer.
rounds.setting: Northern coast -- dramatic sea stacks, crashing surf, dense coconut grove, sea cave with salvage.
rounds.challenge: Decide how to use the opportunity and salvage you found on the northern coast.
rounds.goal: Make the most of the northern coast's resources without taking fatal risks.
rounds.reflection_prompt: You have now survived four full days. What has surprised you most about what it takes to survive? What resources -- physical or mental -- have you relied on most?

scene_hint.location: Rocky northern coast with sea stacks and coconut grove
scene_hint.weather: sunny, surf crashing, sea wind
scene_hint.objects: deflated life raft, flare gun, tin of biscuits, coconut palms, sea cave entrance
scene_hint.character_positions: one survivor examining the life raft, another in a coconut palm, third studying the sea
scene_hint.mood: adventurous but tense, bold optimism mixed with calculated risk

callbacks.text_if_chosen: Your lagoon knowledge means you know water is secured -- you can focus entirely on the raft and food here.
callbacks.text_if_not: Without a confirmed water source, every hour you spend here is an hour your water supply drops.

choices.label: Repair the Life Raft
choices.description: Spend the day patching the raft for a potential sea escape or inter-island signaling.

consequence_scene.headline: Raft Partially Repaired!
consequence_scene.description: It holds air for about two hours. Not enough for open ocean, but useful for coastal signaling. Alex is buzzing with excitement. You burned a lot of energy.

choices.label: Harvest the Coconut Grove
choices.description: Spend the day systematically harvesting coconuts -- food and hydration in one.

consequence_scene.headline: The Coconut Cache!
consequence_scene.description: Forty coconuts cached at camp. Food and water problems are eased for days. Sam is visibly relieved. Alex grumbles about missed rescue opportunities.

choices.label: Study the Currents
choices.description: Use the day to observe tide patterns, current direction, and sea traffic for future planning.

consequence_scene.headline: Critical Navigation Knowledge!
consequence_scene.description: You observe that a southerly current runs past the reef every evening between 5-7 PM. Any raft or signal should be deployed then. Sam marks it in a makeshift journal.

rounds.coaching_moment: Sometimes the bold choice carries risk, but also the highest reward. Weigh carefully.

expert_pick.reason: Leadership experts recommend thinking several moves ahead before committing.

rounds.title: Day 4: The Southern Cliffs (Strategic Path)
rounds.story:
The southern cliffs are everything the bottle message promised. A broad flat-topped rock juts out over the sea -- a natural signal platform. The view is extraordinary: on a clear day you could see a ship fifteen kilometres out. Sam is already calculating the optimal wood arrangement for maximum smoke visibility, speaking quietly but with precision that you are beginning to trust.

But as you explore the clifftop, you discover something unexpected: a rusted metal lockbox wedged in a rock crevice. Old, but solid. Inside, protected by decades of salt corrosion, is a hand-drawn map of the island -- more detailed than anything you could have made yourself -- and a small waterproof notebook filled with survival observations from a previous castaway.
rounds.setting: Southern clifftop with dramatic ocean views. Flat rock platform. Rusted lockbox in a crevice.
rounds.challenge: Balance rescue preparation with the new intelligence from the mysterious lockbox.
rounds.goal: Set up the rescue signal post while extracting maximum value from the discovered artifacts.
rounds.reflection_prompt: You chose the patient, methodical path. What does this say about how you approach uncertain situations in your own life?

scene_hint.location: Southern clifftop with ocean panorama
scene_hint.weather: clear, moderate wind, dramatic clouds on horizon
scene_hint.objects: rusted lockbox, hand-drawn map, waterproof notebook, signal fire wood cache, signal mirror
scene_hint.character_positions: one survivor reading notebook intently, another arranging signal wood, third staring at the ocean
scene_hint.mood: discovery, quiet hope, methodical determination

entries.text: Found freshwater. Key: follow the bird calls at dawn -- they lead to the lagoon northeast of main cove.
Observed Thursday ship pattern. It appears between 0800-1000 from the south. Signal must be visible by 0700 to be safe.
Caves on east coast are safe from all weather. Built permanent fire pit at cliff. Wood cache in the long hollow tree NW of platform.

callbacks.text_if_chosen: Your earlier planning perfectly aligns with what the notebook confirms. You have a head start.
callbacks.text_if_not: The notebook gives you the rescue ship timing you didn't know you needed. Wednesday night preparation is now locked in.

choices.label: Decode the Map -- Explore the Whole Island
choices.description: Use the map to systematically survey island resources you didn't know existed.

consequence_scene.headline: Full Island Intelligence!
consequence_scene.description: The map reveals a freshwater spring, a fruit orchard, and two more caves. You now know this island better than most people know their own neighbourhood.

choices.label: Build the Signal Fire Cache Now
choices.description: Prioritize the rescue mission -- spend the full day building an enormous signal fire cache.

consequence_scene.headline: Signal Cache Complete!
consequence_scene.description: A bonfire's worth of dry wood, coconut husks, and green branches (for black smoke) is cached and ready. Thursday is locked in. Sam calls it 'engineering hope.'

choices.label: Copy the Notebook and Return It
choices.description: Carefully transcribe all the key survival data into your own notes, preserving the original in the box for future castaways.

consequence_scene.headline: Knowledge Preserved
consequence_scene.description: You have the data. And whoever comes after you -- if they need it -- will find the notebook intact. It's a small act that feels enormously human. Sam nods quietly: 'Good call.'

rounds.coaching_moment: Consider how this choice affects your long-term resources, not just the immediate gain.

expert_pick.reason: Calculated risk-taking is what separates growth-oriented leaders from status-quo managers.

rounds.title: Day 4: Building a Real Camp (Fortify Path)
rounds.story:
While Alex and Sam took their separate gambles on the coast, you stayed and transformed the camp into something real. By midday, it has a proper raised sleeping platform off the wet ground, a food cache hanging from a tree to deter insects, a rain-catchment system using the tarp funneled into the metal pot, and a designated cooking fire with wind-break stones.

When Alex and Sam return at sunset -- Alex frustrated, Sam cautiously optimistic -- they stop and stare. 'You built a home,' Sam says quietly. Alex shakes their head but chooses the best sleeping spot without a word. Tonight, everyone sleeps in genuine comfort for the first time. Small victories matter enormously when you have no idea how long this ordeal will last.
rounds.setting: The base camp, now significantly improved. Raised platform, rain catchment, food cache, proper cooking area.
rounds.challenge: Leverage your well-built camp to address the group's next most critical need.
rounds.goal: Use the camp's stability as a foundation for the group's next strategic move.
rounds.reflection_prompt: You chose to invest in the foundation rather than chase immediate opportunities. What were the tradeoffs? Would you make the same choice again?

callbacks.text_if_chosen: Your early shelter instinct was right, and now that philosophy has built something that might last weeks.
callbacks.text_if_not: Today you converted the scrappy first-night camp into something genuinely resilient. It took longer but may matter more.

choices.label: Organize a Food Expedition Tomorrow
choices.description: With camp secured, plan a structured food-gathering mission into the jungle.

consequence_scene.headline: Pantry Stocked!
consequence_scene.description: Papaya, wild yams, and a termite mound (high protein, Sam assures you). The group eats well. Morale climbs sharply when people aren't hungry.

choices.label: Start a Medical Knowledge Session
choices.description: Pool everyone's first-aid knowledge and identify which island plants are medicinal or toxic.

consequence_scene.headline: Island Pharmacopeia!
consequence_scene.description: Sam knows that broad-leaf plantain reduces inflammation. Alex knows how to make a splint. You identify three plant species that are safe to eat. Knowledge now lives in the group, not just one person.

choices.label: Work on a Distress Signal System
choices.description: Create a mirror signal from salvage metal and mark the camp with beach art visible from the air.

consequence_scene.headline: S.O.S. Carved in Stone
consequence_scene.description: A ten-metre S-O-S of white stones on the dark beach. Visible from a low-flying aircraft. And a polished metal signal mirror that can flash over 10 km. Hope made visible.

rounds.image_prompt: a vibrant coastal campsite at sunset, featuring a sturdy raised sleeping platform, a food cache hanging from a tree, and a cooking fire surrounded by smooth stones, warm golden light illuminating the scene
rounds.coaching_moment: Think about trade-offs: what are you giving up to get this benefit?

expert_pick.reason: Leadership experts recommend thinking several moves ahead before committing.

rounds.title: Day 5: The Injury
rounds.story:
Alex slips on a wet rock while gathering firewood and lets out a sharp cry. When you reach them, their ankle is swollen -- possibly sprained, possibly fractured. Alex's face is a mask of frustration and barely concealed panic. 'I'm fine,' they insist through clenched teeth, trying to stand and failing. Sam kneels, examines the ankle with careful hands, and looks at you steadily.

A serious injury changes everything. It reduces the group's work capacity, increases food and water needs for the injured person, and creates an emotional burden that affects morale. How you respond now will shape the group's trust dynamics for the remainder of your time on this island.
rounds.setting: Rocky area near the treeline where Alex fell. Afternoon, hot and humid.
rounds.challenge: Respond to Alex's injury in a way that balances immediate care with group sustainability.
rounds.goal: Manage a group medical emergency with limited resources.

scene_hint.location: Wet rocky area at jungle edge where accident occurred
scene_hint.weather: humid, partly cloudy, recent rain making rocks slick
scene_hint.objects: wet moss-covered rocks, scattered firewood, medical supplies laid out, improvised splint materials
scene_hint.character_positions: injured person sitting against rock holding ankle, one survivor kneeling examining injury, third standing watching with concern
scene_hint.mood: anxious concern, group vulnerability, test of compassion under pressure

callbacks.text_if_chosen: Your medical knowledge session pays off immediately. You know how to assess the injury and construct a proper splint.
callbacks.text_if_not: You do your best with improvised techniques, but better medical preparation would have made this far easier.

callbacks.text_if_chosen: The group trust you built on Day 1 means Alex actually accepts your help rather than pushing you away.
callbacks.text_if_not: Alex's stubborn independence makes giving care harder. Group dynamics matter in moments like these.

choices.label: Full Rest -- Alex Does Nothing for Two Days
choices.description: Insist on complete rest for Alex, redistributing their workload across the group.

consequence_scene.headline: Alex Recovers Properly
consequence_scene.description: Two days of forced rest and Alex's ankle is functional again. The group is exhausted from carrying extra work -- but Alex is visibly grateful. 'I owe you,' they say quietly.

choices.label: Light Duties -- Alex Directs, Not Carries
choices.description: Let Alex contribute mentally -- navigation, planning, camp tasks that don't require walking.

consequence_scene.headline: Alex the Strategist
consequence_scene.description: Forced to think instead of act, Alex turns out to have a surprisingly good mind for logistics. They redesign the food storage system. The injury accidentally revealed a hidden strength.

choices.label: Push Through -- Group Needs Everyone
choices.description: Let Alex decide their own pain threshold and keep working at reduced capacity.

consequence_scene.headline: The Injury Worsens
consequence_scene.description: Alex works through the pain but the ankle deteriorates. Two days later it is significantly worse. Sam gives you a long, quiet look. Some costs compound with time.

rounds.image_prompt: a forest clearing with towering trees and dappled sunlight filtering through leaves, Alex grimacing on the ground beside a pile of firewood, Sam kneeling beside them, concern etched on their face
rounds.coaching_moment: How might your team react to this decision? What about your customers?

expert_pick.reason: Goleman's EQ framework rates empathetic responses as the highest-impact leadership move.

rounds.title: Day 6: Storm Warning
rounds.story:
A crackling, distorted signal -- barely recognizable as human voice -- emerges from a radio salvaged from the wreckage and finally coaxed into partial function by Sam. Through the static, one phrase repeats clearly enough to understand: 'Tropical depression... strengthening... landfall possible... forty-eight hours...'

Sam and you exchange a look. A storm -- potentially a significant one -- in forty-eight hours. Your current shelter may or may not survive it depending on what 'strengthening' means. Alex, ankle still bandaged, is already on their feet. 'We move to the caves,' Alex says. 'Now.' Sam holds up a hand: 'Let's think first.'
rounds.setting: Camp. Late afternoon. The salvaged radio crackles on a flat rock. The sky to the northeast has an unusual yellow quality.
rounds.challenge: Prepare for a potentially severe storm within a tight 48-hour window.
rounds.goal: Optimize your storm preparation given limited time and energy.

scene_hint.weather: deceptively calm, unusual yellow atmospheric tint, distant dark clouds building
scene_hint.objects: crackling salvaged radio, emergency supply pile, tarp shelter, signal mirror, rising wind moving palm fronds

scene_hint.mood: urgent alarm, time pressure, nature's power looming

breaking_news_content.ticker: BREAKING: Tropical depression intensifying -- possible Category 1 landfall in 48-72 hours
breaking_news_content.bulletin: Maritime advisory issued for the region. All vessels advised to seek safe harbor immediately. Island residents warned to prepare for heavy rain, high winds, and storm surge.

choices.label: Relocate Entirely to the Caves
choices.description: Abandon the beach camp and move everything to the eastern cave system for guaranteed storm shelter.

consequence_scene.headline: Caves Weather the Storm
consequence_scene.description: The storm hits hard. Outside, trees bend and break. Inside the cave, you are bone-dry and safe. The right call -- made at the right time.

choices.label: Reinforce Current Shelter
choices.description: Stay and significantly upgrade your existing shelter with every available material.

consequence_scene.headline: Shelter Survives -- Barely
consequence_scene.description: The storm is brutal. One wall collapses and everyone gets soaked before you can repair it. But you endure. At dawn, you look at the wreckage and are grateful it wasn't worse.

choices.label: Stockpile Supplies and Weather It Together
choices.description: Focus on water and food stockpiling before the storm rather than infrastructure -- survival resources outlast bad weather.

consequence_scene.headline: Supplies Saved, Bodies Battered
consequence_scene.description: Everyone gets soaked and cold -- health takes a hit from exposure. But your food and water supply is untouched by the storm. A painful but possibly correct tradeoff.

rounds.title: Day 8: The Second Major Fork
rounds.story:
The storm passed. It was fierce but brief -- a glancing blow rather than a direct hit. In its aftermath, the island looks scrubbed clean and raw. And it has delivered something completely unexpected: a large sealed shipping container has washed directly onto the southern beach, courtesy of the storm surge. It is brightly colored -- clearly from a commercial vessel.

Inside, once Alex forces the latch, you find an extraordinary array of options: a working emergency beacon (EPIRB) with battery life estimated at 72 hours, a cache of MREs (Meals Ready to Eat) and water pouches, a full first aid kit, and a solar-powered emergency communication device that might be able to contact the outside world if you can get it to elevated ground. One person cannot carry everything -- and the beacon, once activated, begins a 72-hour countdown during which a rescue signal will be transmitted. If rescue doesn't come in 72 hours, it goes silent forever.

consequence_scene.headline: Supplies Secured -- But the Wait Is Hard
consequence_scene.description: Sam supports the plan. Alex is barely controlling frustration. You now have excellent resources but two days of knowing rescue is possible yet choosing to wait. It takes a particular kind of discipline.

rounds.title: Day 9: The 72-Hour Wait (Beacon Path)
rounds.story:
The beacon blinks. Hours pass. You find yourself checking it every twenty minutes -- still blinking, still transmitting. Alex has planted themselves on the highest dune, eyes on the horizon, refusing to eat. Sam quietly suggests that maintaining normal survival routines will make the wait psychologically bearable and physically sustainable. The irony is not lost on you: you may be rescued today, or the beacon's battery may die in 72 hours without anyone coming at all.

On hour 36, a radio crackle. A coastguard vessel is in the region investigating the signal but cannot reach your position until tomorrow due to reef navigation risks at night. Hold tight. They are coming.

rounds.goal: Keep the group functional and healthy during the uncertainty of the rescue window.

consequence_scene.description: The group sleeps in shifts, watches the beacon, and wakes sharp and ready. When the rescue boat needs help with a tricky approach, everyone is clear-headed and effective.

rounds.title: Day 9: Direct Contact (Comm Path)
rounds.story:
The solar communication device connects. A calm, professional voice -- a maritime rescue coordinator named Chen -- walks you through the situation. There is a coastguard vessel 180 kilometres away. It can reach you in approximately 20 hours if it departs now. But Chen has a question: there is also a medical evacuation helicopter available if needed, which can reach you in 4 hours -- but it can only carry one person, and its use would delay the ship departure for the vessel.

Alex's ankle is still a concern. Sam has a wound from the storm that is showing early signs of infection. And all of you have lost significant body weight. Is anyone in critical medical need right now?

rounds.title: Day 9: Holding the Line (Wait Path)
rounds.story:
Two days until Thursday. Two days with the EPIRB unactivated, the comm device uncharged, and rescue tantalizingly deferred. Sam's strategic logic is airtight: Thursday's ship combined with the EPIRB signal and the clifftop fire is your strongest possible rescue scenario. But logic and emotion are different languages, and Alex is speaking emotion.

'We have a beacon,' Alex says, voice cracking. 'We have a device. And we're sitting here like idiots.' Sam stays quiet. You are the deciding vote in a two-one group dynamic -- and your decision must hold for two more days of island life.

rounds.title: Day 10: Reflection at Midpoint
rounds.story:
Ten days. You have survived ten full days on an uncharted island with no professional survival training and two people you barely knew before the shipwreck. Your body has adapted -- you move more efficiently, your eyes pick out edible plants automatically now, you sleep through sounds that terrified you on day one. Something has changed inside you too. You are quieter. More deliberate. Less certain of everything and more comfortable with uncertainty.

Sam is writing in a small notebook with a pencil stub. Alex, who you once thought incapable of stillness, is sitting at the water's edge watching a school of fish with what can only be called patience. The island has taught each of you something the other could not have. There is a strange gratitude in that -- complicated, honest, and real.

entries.text: I thought survival was about the body. It turns out it is mostly about the mind. The body will do remarkable things if the mind doesn't give up first.
Alex and Sam taught me things I did not know I needed to learn. Alex taught me that speed matters sometimes. Sam taught me that thinking before moving almost always matters more.
I miss people. I miss noise. I miss choice. But I also notice I am making better decisions than I did ten days ago. Maybe that is the gift inside the ordeal.

consequence_scene.headline: The Real Conversation
consequence_scene.description: Alex is surprised you came. Then open. It turns out the aggression masks real anxiety -- they are as scared as anyone. The conversation changes the remaining days. You face whatever comes next as a genuine team.

consequence_scene.description: You map out the next five days in precise detail. Resources, timings, contingencies. Sam raises an eyebrow: 'You sound like someone who's done this before.' You almost smile. Maybe you have, now.

rounds.title: Day 11: The Unexpected Visitor
rounds.story:
You smell the campfire before you see the person. On the far side of the southern bay, a small fire burns. Someone is already on this island. You approach cautiously. Crouched at the fire is an elderly man -- weathered, lean, clearly comfortable outdoors. He introduces himself as Manu, a fisherman whose boat engine failed five days ago. He has been surviving alone on the eastern side of the island and thought he was alone.

Manu has skills none of you possess: he can read weather from cloud formations, knows which reef fish are safe to eat, and has built a small but elegant fish trap that has been feeding him adequately. But he is elderly and his knee is swollen and painful from a fall. He cannot walk long distances. He could teach you. And he needs your help.

rounds.title: Day 12: The Final Branch
rounds.story:
Rescue is close -- you can feel it in the quality of the coastguard radio transmissions, in Coordinator Chen's increasingly specific questions about your exact location and the reef approach route. It could be tomorrow. It could be in three days. The question now is not whether you will be rescued, but how you use the remaining time and what you carry with you when you leave.

Three distinct paths forward present themselves, each representing a different philosophy about what the final chapter of a survival story should look like. Alex wants action. Sam wants precision. Manu watches all of you with the quiet smile of a man who has already made peace with the island.

rounds.title: Day 13: Rescue Dawn (Signal Path)
rounds.story:
Four hours. That is how long you wait after the confirmation, watching the horizon with the kind of focused attention you now understand is the most human instinct there is: the will to reconnect. At 5:47 AM, a light appears on the horizon. Then another. Then a searchlight sweeps the beach in a slow arc -- methodical, professional, looking for exactly where you are standing.

The coastguard vessel MV Kestrel navigates carefully through the reef channel. A dinghy is deployed. Three crew members approach the beach. The first one steps out, looks at the four of you, and says simply: 'We've got you.'

rounds.title: Day 13: The Reef Navigation (Navigator Path)
rounds.story:
The coastguard captain's voice is steady but careful: the reef approach is the most dangerous part. You have fourteen days of watching these waters. You know the southerly evening current, the submerged rock shelf at 40 metres off the eastern promontory, the safe channel that runs between two sea stacks at the northern edge. What you learned because you had nothing else to do is now the most valuable knowledge on this radio channel.

For forty-five minutes, you guide a professional vessel through waters that most captains would refuse to enter in the dark. 'Left ten degrees. Watch the submerged shelf at your two o'clock. The channel is narrow -- maybe eighteen metres -- between those two rock formations. You are through.'

rounds.title: Day 13: The Document (Legacy Path)
rounds.story:
Seventeen pages. In the hours before rescue arrives, the four of you fill them. Manu draws the fish species, the tide charts, the edible plant markers. Alex -- suddenly practical when given a creative problem -- sketches the reef approach with the eye of someone who ran across it at speed. Sam annotates everything with precision: distances, timings, resource calculations. And you write the introduction, the philosophy of it.

When the coastguard dinghy reaches the beach at dawn and the crew member steps out, you do something unexpected. Before boarding, you walk to the lockbox on the southern cliff and place the document inside alongside the original notebook. Two castaways have now contributed their knowledge to this island. Whoever comes after will not start from zero.
rounds.setting: Beach at dawn, then the clifftop lockbox. A rescue dinghy just arrived.
rounds.challenge: Complete the legacy document and ensure it will survive for future castaways.
rounds.goal: Leave a meaningful legacy before departure -- knowledge that could save a future life.

entries.text: To whoever finds this: the lagoon is 3 km northeast. The caves are east. The rescue ship passes south on Thursdays 0800-1000. The island is survivable. We know because we survived it.
Skills that mattered most: water first, always. Shelter before comfort. Team before ego. Knowledge compounds -- learn something every day.
We are leaving now. The island kept us. But it also taught us. We are grateful for both.

choices.label: Place the Document in the Lockbox
choices.description: Seal the legacy document in the existing lockbox on the southern cliff for future castaways.

consequence_scene.headline: The Chain of Knowledge Continues
consequence_scene.description: The lockbox closes. The cliff holds it. The island holds the cliff. Somewhere in the future, someone who needs it will find it. The crew member who watched the whole thing says nothing -- just nods slowly, once.

choices.label: Give the Document to the Coastguard
choices.description: Hand it to the rescue crew for official maritime safety records.

consequence_scene.headline: Official Maritime Record
consequence_scene.description: The captain accepts it with formality. 'This will be logged with the maritime authority. Reef approach data alone could prevent accidents.' Your knowledge enters official record. A different kind of legacy.

rounds.coaching_moment: Look at your current resource levels — which constraint are you trying to address?

rounds.title: Day 14: Aboard the Kestrel
rounds.story:
The dinghy rocks across the calm morning sea toward the MV Kestrel. You sit in the bow and watch the island shrink. It is smaller than it felt from inside it. It always is. The crew has given each of you a foil blanket, a bottle of clean water, and a bowl of something hot and deliberately unseasoned. You drink the water in long, careful swallows that feel like the best thing you have ever tasted.

In the medical bay, a nurse examines each of you with practiced efficiency. Manu's knee gets attention. Alex's ankle is assessed. Sam's wound is cleaned and properly dressed. When she gets to you, she looks over her clipboard and says: 'Vital signs are surprisingly stable. You took care of yourself out there. That's less common than you'd think.'
rounds.setting: Aboard MV Kestrel. Medical bay, main deck, and bow with island receding behind you.
rounds.challenge: Process the transition from survival mode back to the normal world.
rounds.goal: Complete the physical and psychological transition out of survival mode with clarity and intention.

callbacks.text_if_chosen: The nurse notes the healed abrasions from your Day 1 swim. 'You went into the water after the wreck? Bold.' You nod. It feels like a lifetime ago.
Alex catches your eye across the medical bay and gives you a small, genuine nod. The conversation on Day 10 changed something between you that is still changed.
callbacks.text_if_not: Alex and you sit at opposite ends of the medical bay, each quiet with your own thoughts. Some distances survive rescue.

choices.label: Sleep -- Your Body Has Earned It
choices.description: Accept the crew's offer of a bunk and sleep for the first time in genuine safety.

consequence_scene.headline: Eight Hours of Real Sleep
consequence_scene.description: You wake as the Kestrel enters harbor. Everything hurts less. Your mind is clear. Sam is already sitting up, writing in the notebook. Alex is at the porthole, watching the coastline. It is over.

choices.label: Talk to the Captain About the Island
choices.description: Use the transit time to share everything you know about the island's location and resources with official records.

consequence_scene.headline: Island Officially Charted
consequence_scene.description: Captain Rodriguez takes careful notes. 'We'll flag this location for maritime safety. Your reef data alone is valuable.' The island will appear on future charts -- with your observations contributing to its description.

choices.label: Sit With Manu and Hear His Story
choices.description: Use the journey to learn from Manu's life -- the fisherman who knows things textbooks never will.

consequence_scene.headline: Manu's Fifty Years on the Water
consequence_scene.description: Manu talks for three hours. Storms he survived. Fish that think. The way the sea changes smell before bad weather. When he finishes, you realize you received something that cannot be taught in any classroom.

rounds.image_prompt: a tranquil morning sea with gentle waves reflecting the sun, a small dinghy gliding toward the MV Kestrel, crew members handing out foil blankets and water bottles.
rounds.coaching_moment: Sometimes the bold choice carries risk, but also the highest reward. Weigh carefully.

expert_pick.reason: Goleman's EQ framework rates empathetic responses as the highest-impact leadership move.

rounds.title: Day 15: The Debrief and What Comes Next
rounds.story:
The harbor is full of noise: gulls, machinery, human voices, traffic from the road beyond the dock wall. You have forgotten how loud the normal world is. A maritime authority officer and a counselor meet you at the dock. After the formal debrief -- questions about the MV Meridian's last known position, the wreck site, the island coordinates -- the counselor asks each of you a question that cuts right through the professional veneer of the whole event.

'What did you learn about yourself that you didn't know before?' Alex goes first. Sam goes second. Then it is your turn. You think about every decision, every night, every argument, every coconut, every star you learned to navigate by and every moment you chose patience over panic. The answer is longer than you expected. And more honest.
rounds.setting: Harbor dock, then a coastguard office conference room. Daylight, noise, the world reasserting itself.
rounds.challenge: Articulate the real lessons of the experience and decide how to carry them forward.
rounds.goal: Complete the journey with a clear, meaningful understanding of what survival taught you.
rounds.reflection_prompt: After everything -- what is the single most important decision you made on the island? Not the most dramatic one: the most important one. And what does your answer reveal about your values?

callbacks.text_if_chosen: The counselor notes that your group's survival rate correlates strongly with early cooperative behavior. 'The data on stranded groups consistently shows that early teamwork is the highest predictor of outcome.'
Manu's family is at the dock. His granddaughter runs to him across the concrete. You watch that reunion and feel something clarify inside you.
The officer pauses at one point in the debrief and asks a careful question about the initial rescue resource request. You answer honestly. It is uncomfortable. It is also right.

choices.label: Share Your Story Publicly -- Write About It
choices.description: Commit to documenting the experience to help others understand survival psychology and decision-making.

consequence_scene.headline: A Story Worth Telling
consequence_scene.description: Six months later, your account is read by survival training instructors, school groups, and maritime safety organizations. Three people contact you to say they made different decisions in difficult moments because of what you wrote. The island's lessons multiply.

choices.label: Return to Normal Life -- But Changed
choices.description: Go home, recover, and carry the lessons quietly -- changed but private about it.

consequence_scene.headline: Quietly Different
consequence_scene.description: Your friends notice it within a week. You are slower to react, quicker to listen. You don't explain why. Some things are changed by experience and need no words. You carry the island inside you now.

choices.label: Train in Wilderness Survival -- Turn Experience Into Expertise
choices.description: Enroll in formal survival and wilderness first aid training to formalize what you learned the hard way.

consequence_scene.headline: Expertise Earned Twice
consequence_scene.description: Your survival course instructor pauses when you demonstrate a skill. 'Where did you learn that?' You tell her. She is quiet for a moment. 'Most students learn survival as theory. You have something different -- muscle memory of necessity.' You do.

glossary_terms.definition: The value of the next best alternative you give up when making a decision.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing to spend ₹10,000 on marketing means you can't spend it on hiring staff.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Every resource has competing uses. Smart decision-makers always ask: 'What am I giving up?'
glossary_terms.real_world_example: A student choosing to study for an exam gives up time for leisure — that leisure is the opportunity cost.

glossary_terms.definition: The balance between potential gain and the possibility of loss in any decision.
glossary_terms.example: A bold marketing campaign might attract many new customers — or backfire and damage reputation.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Higher potential rewards usually come with higher risk. The key skill is accurately assessing both sides.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Entrepreneurs take calculated risks when starting businesses, accepting uncertainty for the chance of success.

glossary_terms.definition: Resisting an immediate reward in favor of a larger, later reward.
glossary_terms.example: Investing profits back into training instead of taking them as income now.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research shows people who delay gratification tend to achieve better outcomes. It requires self-control and long-term thinking.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Saving money instead of spending it gives you more buying power in the future.
